evals.prompt:
Run a security audit on this Go HTTP handler:

```go
func uploadHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    file, header, _ := r.FormFile("upload")
    defer file.Close()
    dst, _ := os.Create("/uploads/" + header.Filename)
    defer dst.Close()
    io.Copy(dst, file)
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "Uploaded: %s", header.Filename)
}
```
evals.expected_output: Should identify Go as the stack and load go-general-security.md references. Critical findings: (1) Path traversal — header.Filename can contain '../../../etc/passwd'; must use filepath.Base() and validate against an allowlist. (2) No file size limit — DoS via large upload; must check r.ContentLength and wrap with io.LimitReader. (3) Errors ignored with _ — os.Create and FormFile errors must be handled and returned as HTTP errors. (4) No file type validation — must check magic bytes, not just extension. (5) XSS — fmt.Fprintf reflects filename into response without escaping. Must produce a numbered security report with severity and a corrected version.
assertions: Flags path traversal via header.Filename as Critical
Flags missing file size limit (DoS risk)
Flags ignored errors (_) as security issue
Flags XSS via unescaped filename in response
Produces numbered security report with severity
